text.p: Chilean stocks were expected to open higher Thursday on healthy foreign demand following the sale of a big stake in supermarket chain Santa Isabel to an Argentine group, brokers said.
The blue-chip IPSA index closed Tuesday at 121.92, up 0.68 percent, and the general IGPA index ended 0.36 percent higher at 5402.45. Chilean markets were closed Wednesday for a holiday.
Santa Isabel announced it had reached an agreement with Argentina's Velox Group to sell 37 percent of the chain for $230 million, as Chilean media had reported.
Endesa General Manager Jose Yuraszeck called a news conference for noon local time (1600 GMT) to discuss the Atacama natural gas pipeline, Endesa said.
